title: The Book of Nehemiah Timeline
sub: The Wall Rebuilt in Fifty-Two Days · the Joy of the LORD Is Your Strength
desc: A Persian king's cupbearer leads the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls against mockery, threats, and economic injustice among his own people, culminating in a public reading of the law and a nationwide covenant of renewed commitment.

eras.label: Era One · Nehemiah 1
eras.name: News of Jerusalem's Ruin — a Cupbearer's Prayer
eras.dates: A Persian court official learns of Jerusalem's broken walls and burned gates, and responds with days of fasting and an extended prayer of confession

events.title: The Wall of Jerusalem Lies Breached: Nehemiah's Prayer
events.detail: News that Jerusalem's wall remains broken and its gates burned devastates Nehemiah, a Jewish cupbearer to the Persian king, who responds with days of fasting and a prayer confessing both his own sins and his people's, appealing to God's covenant faithfulness.

verses.text: “O LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of heaven, great and awesome God [El], who keeps his loving covenant with those who love him and obey his commandments.”

eras.label: Era Two · Nehemiah 2
eras.name: Nehemiah Requests Leave — a Night Inspection of the Ruins
eras.dates: Four months after hearing the news, Nehemiah's visible sadness prompts the king to grant him leave to rebuild Jerusalem himself

events.title: The King Grants Nehemiah Leave to Rebuild Jerusalem
events.detail: Noticing Nehemiah's uncharacteristic sadness, the king asks what's wrong; after a quick silent prayer, Nehemiah requests permission and royal letters to travel to Jerusalem and rebuild it, which the king grants.

verses.text: “The king responded, ‘What is it you are seeking?’ Then I quickly prayed to the God [Elohim] of heaven.”

events.title: A Secret Night Inspection: Let's Rebuild the Wall
events.detail: Before telling anyone his plan, Nehemiah secretly inspects the ruined walls by night, then rallies the leaders of Jerusalem to rebuild despite mocking opposition from Sanballat and Tobiah.

verses.text: “The God [Elohim] of heaven will prosper us. We his servants will start the rebuilding. But you have no just or ancient right in Jerusalem.”

eras.label: Era Three · Nehemiah 3
eras.name: The Builders, Gate by Gate
eras.dates: A detailed roster names every family and official who rebuilt a specific section of wall, an entire community working side by side

events.title: Each Worked on the Section Opposite His Own House
events.detail: A detailed, gate-by-gate roster records exactly which families and officials rebuilt each section of the wall, showing an entire community, priests included, working side by side on the section nearest their own homes.

verses.text: “Shallum son of Hallohesh, head of a half district of Jerusalem, worked on the section adjacent to him, assisted by his daughters.”

eras.label: Era Four · Nehemiah 4
eras.name: Ridicule Becomes a Threat of Attack — a Trowel and a Sword
eras.dates: Mockery escalates into a genuine plot of armed attack, met with prayer, a posted guard, and builders working with weapons close at hand. (This chapter's opening six verses belong to the Hebrew text's previous chapter; references here follow the Hebrew numbering, marked inline in the NET text as “(3:33)” and “(4:1)”.)

events.title: Sanballat's Ridicule: Hear, O Our God, for We Are Despised
events.detail: Sanballat mocks the rebuilding effort as something a fox could knock down, and Nehemiah responds not with retaliation but with prayer, asking God to see the builders' reproach. (Numbered 4:1-6 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall he became angry and was quite upset. He derided the Jews.” (Numbered 4:1 in most English translations.)

events.title: Our God Will Fight for Us: Building With a Sword at Their Side
events.detail: When ridicule turns into an actual armed conspiracy against Jerusalem, Nehemiah posts armed guards and has the builders work with a weapon strapped to their side, trusting that God himself will fight for them. (Numbered 4:7-23 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “Wherever you hear the sound of the trumpet, gather there with us. Our God [Elohim] will fight for us!” (Numbered 4:20 in most English translations.)

eras.label: Era Five · Nehemiah 5
eras.name: Economic Injustice Among the Builders
eras.dates: While rebuilding the wall, Nehemiah discovers wealthy countrymen exploiting the poor through debt-slavery and demands it stop immediately

events.title: Each One of You Is Seizing Collateral From Your Own Countrymen
events.detail: Amid famine and heavy taxes, wealthy Jews are charging interest and seizing the children of their poorer countrymen as collateral; Nehemiah publicly confronts them, demands restitution, and models generosity himself by refusing the governor's usual food allowance.

verses.text: “Remember me for good, O my God [Elohim], for all that I have done for this people.”

eras.label: Era Six · Nehemiah 6
eras.name: The Wall Finished in Fifty-Two Days
eras.dates: A final wave of personal threats, false rumors, and a staged prophecy of assassination all fail to stop the project from reaching completion

events.title: The Wall Was Completed in Fifty-Two Days: Our Enemies Were Disheartened
events.detail: Enemies try repeated tricks to lure Nehemiah away or intimidate him into cowardly hiding, including a hired false prophet, but he refuses every ploy and the wall is finished in just fifty-two days: a speed that visibly humbled Jerusalem's surrounding enemies.

verses.text: “When all our enemies heard… they were greatly disheartened. They knew that this work had been accomplished with the help of our God [Elohim].”

eras.label: Era Seven · Nehemiah 7
eras.name: The Register of Returned Exiles Rediscovered
eras.dates: With the wall complete, Nehemiah organizes the city's defense and rediscovers the same genealogical record first compiled generations earlier

events.title: A Faithful Man Who Feared God More Than Many Do
events.detail: With the wall finished but the city still sparsely populated, Nehemiah appoints trustworthy gatekeepers and rediscovers an old genealogical register of the original returning exiles, reproducing it in full as the basis for repopulating Jerusalem.

verses.text: “I put in charge over Jerusalem my brother Hanani and Hananiah the chief of the citadel, for he was a faithful man and feared God more than many do.”

eras.label: Era Eight · Nehemiah 8
eras.name: Ezra Reads the Law — the Joy of the LORD Is Your Strength
eras.dates: The whole community gathers to hear the law read aloud for the first time in a generation, weeping until Ezra and Nehemiah redirect their grief toward joy

events.title: The Joy of the LORD Is Your Strength: the Festival of Shelters Restored
events.detail: Ezra reads the law aloud from dawn to noon before the assembled people, who weep upon hearing it, until Nehemiah and the Levites redirect their mourning into celebration, and the people restore the Festival of Shelters for the first time since the days of Joshua.

verses.text: “Go and eat delicacies and drink sweet drinks and send portions to those for whom nothing is prepared… the joy of the LORD [Yahweh] is your strength.”

eras.label: Era Nine · Nehemiah 9
eras.name: A National Prayer of Confession — Recounting Israel's Whole History
eras.dates: A day of fasting produces the Old Testament's longest single prayer of historical confession, tracing Israel's whole story from creation to the present exile

events.title: You Alone Are the LORD: a Prayer Recounting Israel's Whole History
events.detail: The Levites lead an extended communal prayer tracing Israel's entire history from creation through the exodus, wilderness rebellion, conquest, and repeated cycles of disobedience and rescue, culminating in an honest confession that the present servitude is the fruit of ongoing unfaithfulness.

verses.text: “You alone are the LORD [Yahweh]. You made the heavens, even the highest heavens, along with all their multitude of stars.”

eras.label: Era Ten · Nehemiah 10
eras.name: A Binding Covenant Signed and Sealed
eras.dates: The nation formalizes its confession into a written, signed covenant of specific commitments. (This chapter's opening verse belongs to the Hebrew text's previous chapter, marked inline in the NET text as “(10:1)”.)

events.title: Our Leaders Have Affixed Their Names on the Sealed Document
events.detail: The confession of chapter 9 is formalized into a written, sealed covenant, signed by name by Nehemiah, the priests, the Levites, and the leaders of the people. (The opening verse is numbered 9:38 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “Because of all this we are entering into a binding covenant in written form; our leaders, our Levites, and our priests have affixed their names on the sealed document.” (Numbered 9:38 in most English translations too.)

events.title: We Will Not Neglect the Temple of Our God
events.detail: The covenant's specific commitments are spelled out in detail (no intermarriage, no Sabbath trading, tithes and firstfruits faithfully given) closing with a communal pledge not to neglect the temple of their God.

verses.text: “We will not neglect the temple of our God.”

eras.label: Era Eleven · Nehemiah 11
eras.name: Repopulating Jerusalem — One in Ten
eras.dates: With walls rebuilt but the city still underpopulated, lots are cast to bring a tenth of the nation to live within Jerusalem itself

events.title: One Out of Every Ten to Settle in Jerusalem, the Holy City
events.detail: Since Jerusalem's rebuilt walls still enclosed a sparsely populated city, lots are cast to bring one out of every ten Israelites to live there, with volunteers publicly blessed by the rest of the people for their sacrifice.

verses.text: “The rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of every ten to settle in Jerusalem, the holy city, while the other nine remained in other cities.”

eras.label: Era Twelve · Nehemiah 12
eras.name: Dedicating the Wall With Two Great Choirs
eras.dates: Priestly genealogies lead into the wall's joyful public dedication, celebrated with two massive choirs processing in opposite directions along the ramparts

events.title: Two Great Choirs Give Thanks: Rejoicing Heard From Far Away
events.detail: After a genealogy of the priests and Levites who served since Zerubbabel's day, the completed wall is dedicated with two enormous choirs processing along the wall in opposite directions, meeting at the temple in a celebration of such great joy that it could be heard from far outside the city.

verses.text: “They rejoiced, for God [Elohim] had given them great joy. The women and children also rejoiced. The rejoicing in Jerusalem could be heard from far away.”

eras.label: Era Thirteen · Nehemiah 13
eras.name: Nehemiah's Final Reforms — Remember Me, O My God
eras.dates: Returning from a trip away, Nehemiah finds old compromises creeping back in and enforces a series of sharp final reforms, repeatedly asking God to remember his efforts

events.title: Remember Me, O My God: Sabbath, Tithes, and Intermarriage Enforced Again
events.detail: After a period away, Nehemiah returns to find Sabbath trading resumed, temple provisions neglected, and intermarriage with pagan neighbors creeping back in: he enforces sharp reforms on all three fronts, closing the book with repeated prayers asking God to remember his faithful work.

verses.text: “Remember me for this, O my God [Elohim], and do not wipe out the kindness that I have done for the temple of my God [Elohim] and for its services!”
